decisions.choice: While all DinkusKit stores are dev-only, dependents track dinkuskit/commerce main instead of an exact SHA. A required canary runs on every dinkuskit/commerce PR: it builds template-store and coupons against the PR head and runs their verification, including template-store pnpm verify. A red canary blocks the Commerce merge. Exact pins return only for releases: registry publishes and site deploys record the exact commerce, template-store, and site commits in the Worker version deploy message and registry entry, and that recorded set is the rollback point. Readiness changes from pins current to canary green on the live head. Follow-ups outside this proposal are adding the canary workflow in commerce, switching the dependency spec, and following the same change in coupons.

decisions.choice: Open the store's front door to plain addresses and keep the real guards. (1) The Worker and middleware boundary lets any plain GET or HEAD address (letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore, tilde; not under /api, /_emdash or an underscore or dot prefix) reach the site, which answers not found for anything it does not have; the demo-era approved-address list no longer decides what exists. (2) The word bans on 'admin' and 'setup' anywhere in a path or query are dropped; only EmDash's real /_emdash/admin, /_emdash/api/setup, auth and schema paths are refused, along with dev-bypass, /api/proof, traversal, encoded-dot and null-byte checks, the strict /_emdash and /api allowlists, and the existing method rules. (3) A /[slug] storefront page shows any published Pages entry with the store header and footer, 404s with 'Page not found' otherwise, and Pages gets urlPattern /{slug} in the seed and through the storefront upgrade (an owner-set pattern is kept). decisions.choice: The store upgrades itself, the way EmDash runs its own migrations. (1) The template keeps one ordered list of named storefront upgrades; today: search on Pages, Products and Categories; product fields with optional placeholder art; Pages addresses. Every step only adds or relaxes, never retypes or deletes, keeps owner edits, and is safe to run twice. (2) The first request a Worker isolate serves, after EmDash's own migrations and once EmDash has seeded the store or the owner has set it up (emdash:seed_complete or emdash:setup_complete, the options EmDash checks before it seeds), runs each step not yet recorded and records it in EmDash's options table under dinkus:storefront-upgrades, on whatever database the store runs: D1 on Cloudflare, SQLite locally. Later isolates read that one row and skip. A brand-new store keeps the seed's schema untouched. (3) A step that fails, or a store not yet seeded or set up, is retried after a short back-off; a failure is logged and never fails a shopper's or owner's request. Two isolates racing is harmless because each step checks before it writes. (4) EMDASH_MIGRATIONS_MODE=manual or check turns the self-upgrade off too, as it does EmDash's. (5) The playground is left alone: each visitor's database is seeded fresh from the current seed. (6) pnpm search:upgrade stays as the manual path for a local database and runs the same list. (7) Any future template schema change adds a step to the list in the same PR as its seed change; emdash seed stays first setup only.

decisions.question: How does a store that is already set up pick up the schema changes a newer template makes, on D1 or local SQLite?
decisions.rationale: Ronald locked it 13:18 UTC 28 Oct 2026 (card 'Lock it'), after being told the upgrade now waits for EmDash's seed. His ask, 12:24 UTC: 'We should definitely align ourselves with upstream. I prefer to use D1 for storage. I'd prefer if we handled this now instead of putting it off and forgetting about it.' Template #164's product-field and Pages-address upgrades ran only through scripts/upgrade-storefront-search.ts on a local SQLite file, so a Cloudflare store on D1 (the beta store, every merchant store) had no way to take them. EmDash 1.2 runs its own pending migrations on the first database use per isolate (enforceRuntimeMigrationPolicy, default auto, EMDASH_MIGRATIONS_MODE override) and treats seeding as first setup only; this mirrors that.

decisions.choice: Commerce holds the link (Commerce catalog-page-link-in-commerce-20261029) and the products collection has no commerce_item_id field. (1) The publish check asks Commerce for the page's product (the private catalog route's get by entryId) and sends set-on-sale the page alone. A publish through the content API of a product page Commerce links to no product is refused with a pointer to the Dinkus Commerce panel, as the old rule refused a page with no product id. (2) The shop, categories, search, feeds and product pages read each page's product from Commerce: each public catalog product's page, or the public item route by pageId. On a shipping store a published product page whose product is not on the shop says it is no longer available. (3) While an older store still has the field, a page Commerce holds no link for falls back to the field's value, and the publish check sends that value as catalogItemId, as before. (4) The product-url plugin no longer requires a product id to publish or schedule; it claims a field value only while the field exists, and a schedule grant no longer names a product. (5) The seed drops commerce_item_id; the seeded demonstration pages are known by their slugs. (6) Storefront upgrade 005_commerce_box_off removes the field from an older store only once every published or scheduled product page whose field names a real Commerce product has its link in Commerce. Until then it leaves the field, logs those pages and is tried again later, without holding back later steps. This one step amends template-store-self-upgrade-20261028's 'only adds or relaxes, never deletes'. (7) The playground's Commerce source pin and the paired proof move to the Commerce beta that holds the link, so the playground never runs a Commerce that cannot link a page.

decisions.rationale: Matches Payments (hosted Stripe or Authorize.net only), keeps card data away from agents, and is what Shopify does for agents it does not fully trust.
